Revenue had to be paid even if crops failed due to famine or floods.
Revenue was fixed based on irrigation facilities.

questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. (Average )

answer.value:
Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms:
The Morley-Minto Reforms did not satisfy Indians.
Montagu, the Secretary of State, made a declaration.
The reforms aimed to: Give Indians a greater role in administration; foster self-governing institutions; increase the number of Indian members in the Council of the Secretary of State for India; appoint a High Commissioner for India in London.

The British created new classes to support and justify their rule.

Introduced by Lord Minto in India.
Enacted in response to the Swadeshi Movement and revolutionary activities.
Key features: Increased the number of members in the Imperial Legislative Council; expanded provincial legislative councils; however, the reforms did not bring about radical changes.
